subject: Day 42: six weeks; postpartum visit; crying begins to taper
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 42. Six weeks old. Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit is today. The PURPLE crying curve is at its peak today or has just passed; many families describe this week as the first sustainable inflection.

Action items
- Take the EPDS result and the question list to the postpartum visit; expect a discussion of pelvic floor, mood, exercise clearance, contraception, and breastfeeding. ACOG on the postpartum period: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- If the OB clears exercise, start with walking and pelvic-floor work; running and impact wait one to two more weeks for most uncomplicated deliveries.
- Choose a contraception plan with the OB; lactational amenorrhea is unreliable as a sole method past six months and depends on exclusive breastfeeding. ACOG on postpartum birth control: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-birth-control
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is booked. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Spontaneous smiles to get attention; vowel coos consolidating; head control sustained 30-60 seconds.
- [low concern] Crying near peak intensity today; tapering begins this week or next for most infants.
- [monitor] No social smile by week 8 — note for the 2-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Maternal heavy bleeding, fever, or severe pelvic pain post-visit. Baby cluster of poor feeding plus lethargy plus decreased output.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Tummy time 30 minutes a day cumulative; baby-safe mirror at his eye level motivates head lifts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Read aloud daily with intentional pauses for serve-and-return cadence. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Outdoor stroller walk for 20-30 minutes; varied input for him, cardiovascular recovery for you. AAP HealthyChildren on vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Live singing during routines.

Upcoming
- Day 49: crying typically tapering noticeably.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines.
- Day 70-84: post-vaccine 24-48-hour fussiness window.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
